solucao.p: FALSE. If workers have more bargaining power then the natural rate of unemployment increases

partes.p: [2.5 Points] If unemployment is constantly below its natural level and people expect that inflation will be the same as last year's inflation the inflation rate explodes over time (that is, it increases over time).

solucao.p: If $u_{t} - u^{n} > 0$ for all $t$ then $\pi_{t} > \pi_{t-1}$ and inflation explodes.

partes.p: [2.5 Points] A negative financial shock in the IS-LM model shifts the IS curve to the left.

solucao.p: TRUE. A negative financial shock in the IS-LM model reduces investment for a given interest rate. This represents a shift of the IS curve to the left. Consider a modified version of the Solow Model with technological progress that includes human capital.

partes.p: [2.5 Points] Adding human capital to the Solow model doesn't change steady state growth.

solucao.p: TRUE. Steady state growth is given by the rate of technological progress, regardless of the presence of human capital.

partes.p: [2.5 Points] Human capital doesn't influence the level of output per worker in steady state.

solucao.p: FALSE. Even though human capital does not change steady state growth, it affects the level of output per worker in steady state.

partes.p: [2.5 Points] If we assume no difference in productivity across countries, the model predicts higher inequality in output per worker than we observe in the data.

solucao.p: FALSE. If we assume no difference in productivity across countries, the model predicts lower inequality than we observe in the data.

partes.p: [2.5 Points] On average, poor countries grow faster than rich countries.

solucao.p: TRUE. On average poor countries are further from their steady state than rich countries, so they tend to grow faster.

partes.p: [5 Points] Let $k_{t+1}$ be the capital per worker. Derive the law of motion for $k_{t}$. That is, express $k_{t+1}$ as a function of $k_{t}, s, n, \delta$ , and $\alpha$ . (Hint: divide by $N_{t}$ on both sides, and use $k_{t+1}n \approx k_{t}n)$
[5 Points] Find the steady state level of $k_{t}$, denote it $k^{*}$. How does it depend on $\delta$ ? Provide an economic intuition.

solucao.p: It depends negatively on $\delta$ : if capital depreciates at a faster rate then the level at which it will be constant is lower.
